Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.75% today to $371.05, extending a sharp two-week decline of 1.58%. The drop comes as crude oil prices have retreated significantly—U.S. oil dropped to $89.53 per barrel today from over $100 just days ago—which directly pressures refiner margins. Refinery utilization remains strong at 95.7%, but refiners profit from the gap between what they pay for crude and what they sell refined products for; when crude prices fall faster than refined product prices can follow, margins compress and stock prices tend to sink.

Geopolitical risk in the Middle East, highlighted by Iran's recent attacks on U.S. positions in the Gulf, had been supporting oil prices earlier in the week. However, the broader pullback in crude suggests that concern has faded or been overtaken by other factors—possibly weakening demand signals or profit-taking after a period of elevated prices. This kind of reversal is typical when fear premium drains out of the market.
